title: UTM Converter: Zone, Easting and Northing
description: Convert latitude/longitude to UTM zone, easting and northing with the UTM Converter — WGS84, both hemispheres, metres exact. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, Times Square converts to zone 18N, easting 585,633 m, northing 4,512,388 m — and London to 30U, 699,331 E, 5,710,142 N, each point at home in its own 6-degree strip of the world.
quick_answer: The UTM Converter translates WGS84 coordinates into Universal Transverse Mercator zone, easting and northing — and converts UTM values back to latitude and longitude. Enter a pair and read its position in metres within its zone: the grid that mapping, military and field-science work runs on worldwide.

body.t: Plots, transects and sample points are logged in UTM across ecology, geology and archaeology. Convert GPS pairs before the field notebook hardens. MGRS strings build on this — see the
A CSV of eastings and northings needs its zone to mean anything. This converter verifies single points so the batch import can be trusted.
UTM is the substrate under MGRS and much allied mapping — fluency here is fluency everywhere in that world.
Topographic maps print UTM grid ticks in their margins. Converting your point explains which blue numbers your pencil should chase.

Denver converts to 13S, easting 500,831 m — nearly the 500,000 false easting itself, because Denver sits almost on zone 13's central meridian (−105°). An easting near 500,000 means 'near the zone's spine'; near 100,000 or 900,000 means 'near its edge'.
Sydney converts to 56H, northing 6,250,948 m — southern-hemisphere northings count down from a 10,000,000 m false origin at the equator, so the number itself announces the hemisphere.

popular_table.note: Norway and Svalbard bend the zone map (zones 31V–37X have famous exceptions) so their land stays in fewer zones — the converter follows the standard, exceptions included.

faq: Which hemisphere letter or N/S suffix?
Northings need the hemisphere to be unambiguous: state it (or the band letter, which implies it). An easting/northing pair without zone and hemisphere is an address with no town.
The transverse Mercator series used is accurate to centimetres within a zone — far beyond consumer GPS. Legal work still follows survey procedure and datums.
Edge of a zone — which one wins?
A point within a whisker of a boundary converts in either zone; professionals keep a whole project in ONE zone (the one containing most of it) even past the edge.
Shrinking the central meridian slightly spreads distortion evenly — nowhere in a zone does scale error exceed about 1 part in 1,000. The bargain every transverse Mercator makes.
Store the original pair; UTM is a working projection. Zones make UTM values ambiguous without metadata, while lat/lon is the universal original.
Zone 32V extends west over Norway, deleting most of 31V/33V's land work, and Svalbard's zones are specially widened — documented quirks the converter honours.
Never inside a zone (the false easting prevents them) — a negative easting in the wild is a sign error or another system's value.
